description: Redo AI product photo and video examples from your own photo: a desk photo, or a short ad with an actor, voice, and captions. Credits (plan units) show first.
h1: See It. Recreate It. AI Product Photo and Video Examples
lead: These AI product photo and video examples start from a scene you would already post. The desk card has the room and the crop. Drop in the mug you sell, and that quiet setting comes back as your file. A short ad from the still is a separate file.
card: Six product photos you can recreate, from a travel mug to a sunscreen tube, plus a way to start a short ad.
intro: You can see the size and the setting before you spend a credit. The tote card puts the bag beside clothes so a shopper can judge the size. Use your own tote in that frame. Turn the still into a short ad when you want motion, and the credit cost is on screen first.
steps_h2: How to Recreate an Example in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: You get your own version of a scene you would actually post. Upload the item you sell, open the card, and take the file home.

steps.d: Upload one photo of the whole mug, tote, shoe, or tube you ship. A product page works when its pictures show that same item.
Open the card whose room and crop match the post you would run. The desk, the outfit, or the daylight frame is already chosen.
Check the item against what you ship, then save the photo or publish the short ad.

faq.q: What is an AI product photo example?
faq.a: It is a finished photo with the room and the crop already chosen, not an empty box. One card is a desk and a mug. You bring the item you sell. A short ad is a later file, after that still matches the item in your box.

faq.q: How does an example become my file?
faq.a: Paste the product page or upload one photo, then type the one sentence the ad should say. For the sunscreen tube, the photo of the whole tube is enough. A photo costs 24 credits, and a 15-second video costs 60. The cost shows before anything runs.

faq.q: Why use an example instead of hiring a creator?
faq.a: You can try a second opening without waiting on a creator's calendar. A shop with a knit running shoe can drop yesterday's photo into the feed card, then make another file that opens on a different line. Each file is its own credit charge.

A one-person shop packing orders at night gets the most from these cards. A marketer who must hand a client a file this week uses them the same way. A brand that already photographs every product in a studio can skip this set.

faq.q: Can I use an example if I have never edited video?
faq.a: Yes. A photo of the whole item and one open card are enough. You type one line, and the spoken words are filled in from that. A short ad can use one of 53 AI actors. There is no timeline to learn before the first file.

Small packages and larger ones both fit. A travel mug, a tote, a vase, a wallet, a running shoe, and a sunscreen tube each have a card. Pick the crop that fits the item, then compare the file with what you ship.

faq.q: Can the product come from a photo I took?
faq.a: Yes. The item in the file comes from the photo you upload, or from a product page you paste. Show the whole product, including the lid or the sole. See [URL to video](page:url-to-video) when you start from a link.

faq.q: Where can I post the file?
faq.a: Most shops post the tall 9:16 file first, because it fills a phone. Use 1:1 when the placement is a square feed, and 16:9 when the placement is wide. 4:3 and 3:4 are there when a slot asks for them. Post it on your social account, or download it for the store.

faq.q: Do I pay to make a file from an example?
faq.a: Yes. The pictures here only show the look. A file you make spends credits on a paid plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. You see the cost before the job starts. A failed job returns those credits.

faq.q: Can I use the file in ads and client work?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark, so it can run as a paid ad and sit on your product page. A file you make for a client is the same kind of download. You still follow the ad account's rules on what the video may claim.

faq.q: Why not build the ad from a blank page?
faq.a: A blank page makes you invent the desk, the crop, and the first line at the same time. The desk card already chose the room. You only decide whether the item in the photo is yours, and what the voice should say.
